say: Check the spelling of the first word on that line. Python only knows it when it is spelt exactly right.
sayAgain: The word should be p, r, i, n, t. Compare yours letter by letter.

say: Python cares about capital letters. Look at the first letter of that line.
sayAgain: The instruction is written all in small letters.

say: Python thinks one of your words is a name it should already know. Text needs quotes around it.
sayAgain: Look at the line in the error message. Is every piece of text inside a pair of quotes?

say: Something on that line was opened but never closed. Count the brackets and the quotes.
sayAgain: Every opening bracket needs a closing bracket, and quotes come in pairs.

say: One of your lines needs to print two things. What goes between two things inside the brackets?
sayAgain: Look at line 2 of the example in the guide to see how two pieces of text share one print.
